To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT: Brian’s Monday morning brief — casuals’ pay and Kisumu loading

Brian,

Thanks for taking this on while I’m away. I know you’ll be at Embakasi from 5:30, and you know the team. The main thing is to go in straight with them: this is our mess, not theirs. They worked, they were due to be paid on Friday, and they have every reason to be upset. Please don’t go in defensive or ask them to be patient as if they’ve done something wrong.

I’ve put the facts, what we can say, and a plan for the morning below. This is a draft for us to check before Monday.

What happened to Friday’s pay

The bank rejected the entire Friday bulk payment file at validation because the beneficiary reference column was too long for its new template. None of the 212 payments in that file was processed. Finance only saw the rejection after 5pm because the alert went to the old finance mailbox, by which time the bank cut-off had passed. Kevin has accepted that this was a Finance failure.

Njeri has approved payment through M-Pesa instead. Kevin’s realistic expectation is for the money to reach phones on Monday by 11am, subject to getting the numbers right and the batch going through. This is the expectation we have, not a confirmed completion. Please check the status with Kevin on Monday rather than assuming it has been sent or received.

Njeri has also approved KES 500 per person for Monday lunch and fare for every casual on the affected list. It is to be paid in the same M-Pesa batch. The company will cover the M-Pesa charges; nothing should be deducted from anyone for those charges.

What to say to the team

Please apologise in person on behalf of management, as Njeri asked. You can use your own words, but something along these lines:

“Good morning. I’m sorry that you were not paid on Friday. You did your work and we failed to get your pay to you when we should have. The bank rejected the payment file and none of those payments went through. We did not pick up the rejection in time to fix it before the bank cut-off. That is on us.

“We have approved payment by M-Pesa. Finance expects the money to reach phones on Monday by 11am, but I cannot tell you it has landed until we have confirmation. There is also KES 500 for Monday lunch and fare for each person on the affected list, in the same batch, and we will pay the M-Pesa charges. Peninah will be here from 7:30 with the list to help check numbers and payslips.

“I know you need your money, not just an explanation. I’ll keep you updated on what we know and what we’re doing, including if anything changes.”

Please don’t promise “by lunch”, a time earlier than 11am, or that everyone will receive payment by 11am regardless of their number or the batch status. Remember Mombasa in 2024: the supervisor said “by lunch”, the money came at 4pm and half the shift sat down. We cannot repeat that. Equally, don’t say the batch has been sent or that anyone has been paid unless Kevin or the individual has confirmed it.

You can promise the apology, the approved KES 500 and company-paid charges, that we will check the numbers, and that you will give honest updates. If the 11am expectation changes, tell them promptly and give the next update when you have a reliable one. Don’t fill a gap with a guess.

Before the group discussion

Please speak to Ouma privately first, before addressing everyone. He is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent to think about; listen to what he and the others are worried about without treating him as the problem. Tell him the same facts you will give everyone else, including that 11am is an expectation, not a guarantee. Ask what the group needs to know and whether he is willing to help make sure people hear the update. Don’t put him under pressure to make promises on their behalf.

Joseph says people are talking about refusing to load the Kisumu trucks until they see money. Please also speak to him early so you understand the mood and can agree how updates will reach the whole shift. The trucks need to leave by 9am for the mill’s offloading slot, which is before the expected pay time. We must plan for that gap rather than imply payment will arrive before departure.

Numbers and individual questions

Peninah has confirmed 198 numbers; she could not reach 14 people, mostly new loaders from the Athi River intake. She’ll be at Embakasi from 7:30 with the printout. Please make sure those 14 know to see her and have a quiet, orderly way to give her their correct numbers face to face. She’ll also have her laptop for anyone who wants a printed payslip.

Ask Kevin and Peninah to coordinate on how corrected numbers get into the batch and what happens if someone cannot be reached or a payment fails. Don’t assure those 14 that correcting a number at 7:30 automatically means their money will arrive by 11. If someone’s pay has not arrived, take their details through Peninah and get a specific follow-up from Finance rather than asking them simply to wait.

If Ouma’s group refuses to load

Stay calm and listen. Don’t argue with the group, threaten anyone’s contract or dismissal, or single Ouma out. Our procedure is clear: a stoppage is handled by Operations and HR together, and no one is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day.

Contact HR immediately and handle the response jointly. Explain the pay position honestly, hear the group’s concerns and agree when you will update them again. Grievances can go through Joseph as shift supervisor and then to HR within 48 hours, but don’t use that route to avoid responding to a stoppage on the ground.

At the same time, assess with Operations what can safely and realistically be loaded and whether the 9am departure or mill slot is at risk. Alert the relevant transport and mill contacts early if there may be a delay; don’t wait until 9am to discover we have missed the slot. Do not promise the trucks will leave on time if you don’t know, and don’t pressure anyone with threats to make it happen.

WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes. I’m up from 4:30; my flight is at 7:05, so please message early if there is a change in the payment plan or the situation at the depot. I know Peninah arrives after I’m due to leave, so please keep HR involved on the ground for anything that develops later.

Thanks, Brian. Be straight with the guys and keep them informed, even when the update is that we’re still waiting for confirmation.
